items.title: Iran threatens new offensive while US rules out extending ceasefire deal
items.summary: DUBAI/WASHINGTON: Iran will shift to a "fully offensive" military posture because efforts to negotiate a permanent end to the war with the US have stalled, a senior Iranian official told Reuters on Monday, as Washington ruled out extending a temporary ceasefire agreement. A memorandum of understanding signed in June to end the war had given Iran and the US until Monday to reach a final peace agreement. Asked by reporters on Monday if the US was seeking to extend June's interim agreement, US President Donald Trump said no.

items.title: Trump approval falls to 33 pct, lowest of his presidency
items.summary: WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump's approval rating fell to the lowest level of his presidency, with an overwhelming majority of Americans concerned the US war with Iran will last a long time, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll that concluded on Monday. Just 33 per cent of respondents in the four-day survey said they approved of Trump's performance in the White House, while 64 per cent disapproved. Some 80 per cent of Americans – including 87 per cent of Democrats and 71 per cent of Republicans – think US involvement in Iran "will go on for an extended period of time," the Reuters/Ipsos poll found.

items.title: Trump says North Korea's Kim has responded to his overtures
items.summary: WASHINGTON: A day after he ordered the United States to scale back military exercises with South Korea and called North Korea "unthreatening and respectful", US President Donald Trump said on Monday that North Korean leader Kim Jong Un had responded to his outreach. North Korea denounces such drills as preparations for war. Kim and Trump's relationship was a dominant theme during Trump's first term.

items.title: UK PM exchanged messages with Trump aide imposter
items.summary: LONDON: New British Prime Minister Andy Burnham exchanged messages with someone posing as Susie Wiles, the White House chief of staff, several media outlets reported on Monday. The incident was deemed serious enough for the British embassy in Washington to raise the matter with the White House, according to two sources cited by Politico. Burnham succeeded former Labour Party leader Keir Starmer as prime minister on July 20.

items.title: 'Rest in Power': Thousands gather in London for vigil honouring academic Arday
items.summary: LONDON: Thousands attended a vigil in central London on Monday for Jason Arday, a former University of Cambridge sociology professor who was found dead on Friday after weeks of intense scrutiny over accusations of plagiarism and other claims. Arday, once hailed as Cambridge's youngest Black professor, resigned on Aug 5 after a former researcher accused him of plagiarism in his PhD thesis. Arday denied the allegation but acknowledged making mistakes.

items.title: White House attacks CNN reporter for question on Trump aide
items.summary: During an event in the Oval Office, reporter Kristen Holmes asked Trump, 80, to respond to comments by a Democratic lawmaker about the president's executive assistant Natalie Harp, 35. "Someday, your children will come across your disgusting and inhumane question," the White House's "Rapid Response" team said in an X post directed at Holmes and linking to a video of Trump's response. "You're a loud, boisterous person, you're fake news, be quiet," Trump said to Holmes.

items.title: Trump envoy says Hamas disarmament could begin within 30 days
items.summary: JERUSALEM: US President Donald Trump's envoy Jared Kushner said Monday that progress towards disarming Hamas and moving forward with a Gaza peace plan could begin within a month, after meeting with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. The comments came as Kushner and Netanyahu agreed that an American general would verify Hamas's disarmament, an Israeli official said, as the premier insisted there would be no Israeli pullout from Gaza until then. The two sides "agreed that no redeployment or reconstruction would take place in the Gaza Strip before Hamas is disarmed throughout Gaza," a senior Israeli official told AFP.

items.title: Umno youth leaders want clarity on Auku replacement [WATCH]
items.summary: They said students should have greater freedom to speak, think critically and take part in democratic life. However, they said scrapping Auku without a clear replacement could leave universities facing uncertainty over governance, discipline and accountability. Pokok Sena Umno Youth chief Mohd Farhan Ahmad said the reform should give students more freedom to express differing views and engage in constructive debate.

items.title: Explainer: What makes a by-election necessary in Malaysia, and when it is not?
items.summary: By-elections are held when a seat falls vacant for reasons other than the dissolution of Parliament. Article 54(1) of the Federal Constitution requires a by-election to be held within sixty days from the time the EC gets notified about a vacant seat. A seat becomes vacant if the incumbent resigns, gets expelled, passes away or gets disqualified from holding office.

items.title: Georgia man charged in US with running US$165 million crypto Ponzi scheme
items.summary: NEW YORK: A Georgia man has been deported from Fiji to face charges in his home state accusing him of defrauding more than 6,000 investors and causing more than US$165 million of losses in a cryptocurrency Ponzi scheme, the US attorney in Atlanta said on Monday. Edward Zimbardi, 59, of Flowery Branch, Georgia, was indicted on 12 counts of wire fraud, 12 counts of money laundering and one count of money laundering conspiracy. Prosecutors said Zimbardi pitched The Crypto Program as a means to purchase online advertising packages, offering a guaranteed 25 per cent monthly rate of return on an initial US$550 investment.

items.title: Trump sends shock waves by cutting drills with South Korea
items.summary: WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump's decision to scale back military drills with close ally South Korea sends an alarming message at a time when the US military is being stretched by the Iran war. Trump announced Sunday that he told the Pentagon to scale back "inappropriate and hostile" yearly military drills with South Korea, hours before they were to begin on Monday. Trump said the exercises were "costly" and inappropriate because Kim had always been "unthreatening and respectful" to him.

items.title: Russia summons Japan ambassador over disputed islands row
items.summary: MOSCOW: Moscow said Monday it had summoned the Japanese ambassador after Tokyo condemned President Vladimir Putin's recent visit to Russia's far-eastern Kuril Islands, which are also claimed by Japan. Moscow retaliated by summoning Japanese envoy Akira Muto. "We have summoned the (Japanese) ambassador," Lavrov told reporters, adding that Tokyo had initially said Muto could not attend immediately.

items.title: Paramount demands US$1.9 billion surety over states' merger lawsuit
items.summary: LOS ANGELES: Paramount Skydance is demanding California and other US states suing to block its merger with Warner Bros. put up US$1.9 billion to cover fees the company will have to pay if the deal gets delayed, according to a lawsuit filed Monday. Paramount, which is run by David Ellison, whose ultra-wealthy family is a close ally of US President Donald Trump, launched a US$110 billion bid for control of a stable of assets that includes Warner Bros. Pictures, CNN and the HBO Max streaming service. Monday's filing reflects the pressure on Paramount, with a US$7 million-a-day "ticking fee" due to kick in for Warner Bros. shareholders if the takeover is not complete by Oct 1.

items.title: 'Road crashes costing Malaysia RM30b yearly'
items.summary: MALAYSIA incurs up to RM30 billion in socioeconomic losses each year due to road accidents, said Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi. He said last year alone, road accidents claimed 6,537 lives, equivalent to an average of 18 deaths a day. Nanta said 80.6 per cent of accidents were due to human factors.

items.title: Factors behind lower birth rates
items.summary: DELAYED marriage, rising living costs and postponement of pregnancy are among the factors contributing to Malaysia's declining fertility rate. National Population and Family Development Board director-general Datuk Abdul Shukur Abdullah said the total fertility rate fell from 2.1 children in 2010 to 1.6 in 2022. Shukur said Malaysia was projected to become an aged nation by 2036.

items.title: Thailand's second-quarter GDP grows 1.9pc year-on-year
items.summary: BANGKOK: Thailand's economy grew 1.9 per cent in the second quarter of 2026 from a year earlier, official data showed yesterday, higher than the median forecast of 1.7 per cent in a Reuters poll of analysts. In the January-March quarter, growth was 2.8 per cent on the year and a revised 0.6 per cent on the quarter. For the whole of 2026, the agency predicted the economy to grow 2.0 to 2.5 per cent, compared with a previous forecast of 1.5 to 2.5 per cent growth.

items.title: Ebola outbreak claims 2,325 lives in Democratic Republic of Congo
items.summary: THE Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has killed 2,325 people, government data showed on Sunday, surpassing the toll from the 2018-2020 outbreak to become the deadliest in the country's history. Democratic Republic of Congo's public health institute said in its latest report confirmed cases had risen to 4,945. There are now 4,945 confirmed cases, the data showed.

items.title: Police seize RM1.66mil contraband cigarettes, arrest two
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police arrested two men believed to be involved in a syndicate storing and distributing contraband cigarettes, with items worth RM1.66 million seized during Ops Taring Alpha 1 in the Klang Valley today. "In total, we seized 2,115 cartons of various brands of suspected unpaid duty cigarettes, along with two vehicles and five mobile phones believed to be connected to the illegal activities," he said in a statement today. Zaki said the value of the seized cigarettes and goods was RM1,499,852, while the total value of all seizures, including related assets, was RM1,661,352.

items.title: Strong political will from top leadership key to fighting corruption, says Ayob Khan
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Strong political will, starting from the highest level of leadership, is crucial to combating corruption and strengthening integrity, says former deputy inspector-general of police Tan Sri Ayob Khan Mydin Pitchay. He said top leaders must lead by example and demonstrate firm resolve, as organisational transformation would only succeed if those at the helm sent a clear message of zero tolerance for misconduct. "Change must come from the top.

items.title: Pakistan detains 258 foreigners in scam centre raid
items.summary: ISLAMABAD: Pakistan authorities said Monday they detained 258 foreigners, including 40 Chinese nationals, following a raid on an alleged "scam call centre" in the capital Islamabad. "They were running a scam call centre in Gulberg Green, a housing society on the outskirts of Islamabad," an official from the Federal Investigation Agency, a Pakistani intelligence service, told AFP. Media reports said the foreigners were detained last week.

items.title: Japan sets sights on the moons of Mars
items.summary: JAPANESE scientists are readying a mission to Mars' moons to retrieve samples that may unlock the origins of the Solar System and life on Earth, although a rival Chinese mission aims to make it back first. The unmanned Martian Moons eXploration (MMX), set to blast off from Tanegashima Space Centre in the coming months, could also lay the groundwork for humans visiting the red planet. The spacecraft will also observe Demios, the other of Mars' moons — but without landing — before a return capsule heads back to Earth to land in Australia in around 2031.

items.title: Today's news in pictures - Monday, August 17, 2026
items.summary: MISSED what happened today? Here's a glimpse at what happened throughout the country in photographs. [[nid:1513339]] [[nid:1513338]] [[nid:1513337]] [[nid:1513336]] [[nid:1513335]] [[nid:1513334]] © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: UK's media-savvy PM shifts messaging to TikTok, podcasts
items.summary: WHETHER he is pulling a pint, tossing a builder's helmet in the air or running with Olympic medallist Mo Farah, the United Kingdom's new Prime Minister Andy Burnham has embraced social media with a deft touch. Compared with predecessor Keir Starmer, "Burnham has a far more astute communications team around him" with a "better grasp of the media environment", said Steven Buckley, a lecturer in digital media sociology at City St George's, University of London. 10 Downing Street, Burnham addressed a crowd including teenage influencers invited because they make TikTok clips about Labour politics.

items.title: NST Leader: Of Tabung Haji and 'bleeding assets'
items.summary: TABUNG Haji is defending its loss-making investment in Great Minster House in the United Kingdom while property experts are questioning its "low" returns. Great Minster House isn't the only property Tabung Haji holds in the UK. The focus should not be whether Tabung Haji made a bad investment simply because Great Minster House suffered valuation losses.

items.title: Two-minute Genting jewellery heist nets nearly RM1.7mil
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Three men took barely two minutes to carry out a jewellery heist at Sky Avenue, Genting Highlands, making off with nearly RM1.7 million worth of jewellery and gold bars this morning. Acting Pahang police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob said initial investigations showed the suspects had driven up to the hilltop resort to carry out the robbery. "They took about two minutes to carry out the robbery.

items.title: Fuel tanker driver to be charged tomorrow over fatal Temerloh crash
items.summary: TEMERLOH: The fuel tanker driver involved in the crash that killed a mother and son at Km9 of Jalan Temerloh-Triang near Kampung Lebak here on Aug 14 will be charged tomorrow. District police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Nasyim Bahron said the man would be charged under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 for causing death by reckless or dangerous driving. Nasyim said a urine screening conducted on the driver returned negative for drugs.

items.title: Trump threatens to bomb Oman if it gets in way of Iran deal
items.summary: WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump on Monday threatened to bomb Oman if it "gets in the way" of a US deal with Iran on the Strait of Hormuz and called for Iran to surrender. "If Oman gets in the way, we'll bomb the shit out of them," Trump told Fox News journalist Trey Yingst, referring to ongoing talks between Oman and Iran on control of the strait, while Washington is also pursuing its own talks. On Friday, Trump claimed that he would even declare the Strait of Hormuz part of US territory, while Iran retorted that the crucial energy waterway it has blockaded "will remain Iranian."

items.title: Firefighters battle 2.8ha hill forest blaze near Shah Alam mosque
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: A 2.8ha hill forest near the Sultan Salahuddin Abdul Aziz Shah Mosque in Section 14 here caught fire this afternoon. Selangor Fire and Rescue Department assistant director (Operations) Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the department received an emergency call at 1.01pm and dispatched a team to the scene. "Firefighters from the Shah Alam Fire and Rescue Station found about 2.8ha of hilly forest ablaze upon arrival.

items.title: Tahfiz teacher jailed 11 years, caned 12 strokes for abusing three students
items.summary: AYER KEROH: A tahfiz teacher was sentenced to 11 years' jail and 12 strokes of the cane by the Sessions Court today after pleading guilty to 10 charges of unnatural sex and sodomy involving three students. Muhammad Aimanuddin Julaihi, 31, who was unrepresented, pleaded guilty after the charges were read to him before judge Rohatul Akmar Abdullah. Rohatul sentenced the accused to 10 years' jail and one stroke of the cane for each of the first eight charges, and 11 years' jail and two strokes of the cane for each of the two sodomy charges.

items.title: 'Aku Berjanji' to ignite patriotic spirit, says Fahmi
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The National Day and Malaysia Day (HKHM) 2026 theme song, "Aku Berjanji", is set to strengthen the spirit of patriotism and love for the country, says Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. Fahmi, in a Facebook post today, urged Malaysians to listen to and embrace the song, composed and performed by renowned singer Faizal Tahir. Earlier, Fahmi received Faizal in Putrajaya, where the singer also briefed him on his upcoming concert on Oct 3 at Unifi Arena, Bukit Jalil.

items.title: RTS Link enters final countdown with high-tech security systems in place
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: The Johor Baru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link has entered its final stretch, with major infrastructure at Bukit Chagar station largely in place ahead of its scheduled Jan 1, 2027 opening. Malaysia Rapid Transit System Sdn Bhd (MRTS) project director Zulkifli Mohamed said the station was equipped with advanced security and passenger-processing systems to support safe and efficient cross-border travel. "The Bukit Chagar station features real-time monitoring capabilities, allowing operations and security teams to monitor activities and respond immediately to any incidents.

items.title: Selangor waits for Putrajaya to register Myanmar refugees before deciding next steps
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 17 — The Selangor government is awaiting the Home Ministry’s registration of Myanmar refugees and stateless individuals under the Refugee Registration Document (DPP) before deciding on further measures to manage the community in the state. Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said the state government was currently compiling data on the community at the district level to be submitted to the Home Ministry, enabling follow-up action to be taken with relevant agencies and the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR). He said the state government had no authority to issue licences or permits to the community to carry out certain activities, as the matter fell under the jurisdiction of the Federal Government, particularly the Home Ministry.

items.title: Viral sword threat in Langgar lands Kedah-born man in Perlis police custody for three days
items.summary: KANGAR, Aug 17 — Police detained a 46-year-old man over a viral social media post allegedly containing a threat to injure an individual with a sword. Perlis acting police chief SAC Zaihairul Idrus said the Kedah-born suspect was detained in Langgar yesterday and remanded for three days from today. “Police recovered the sword shown in the viral post from the suspect’s vehicle during the arrest.

items.title: No licence, no insurance, so no Mercedes: Langkawi JPJ seizes Bangladeshi farmer’s luxury ride
items.summary: ALOR SETAR, Aug 17 — The Kedah Road Transport Department (JPJ) seized a Mercedes-Benz vehicle used by a Bangladeshi man during Ops Luxury around Jalan Padang Matsirat, Langkawi, yesterday. In a statement today, Kedah JPJ director Stien Van Lutam said the 38-year-old man, who works as a vegetable farmer, had been using the vehicle since May 27, 2025. “Checks revealed that he did not have a valid driving licence, while the motor vehicle licence (LKM) had expired and the vehicle had no insurance coverage, which lapsed on July 26,” he said, adding that the vehicle was subsequently seized.

items.title: RM3.4m bill stands for former MARA Corp CEO after appeal fails over 25 hires
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 17 — The Court of Appeal has upheld the High Court’s decision in ordering Majlis Amanah Rakyat Corporation Sdn Bhd (MARA Corporation) former group chief executive officer (CEO) Datuk Badlisyah Abdul Ghani to pay RM3.4 million to the company for breaching his contractual, fiduciary and statutory duties. A three-man bench comprising Justices Datuk Wong Kian Kheong, Datuk Ahmad Kamal Md Shahid and Datuk Ahmad Fairuz Zainol Abidin had dismissed Badlisyah’s appeal and affirmed the High Court’s decision. The court also ordered Badlisyah to pay RM50,000 in costs.

items.title: High Court lets Aliff Syukri defer apology to ex-minister Abdul Kadir in RM30m investment suit pending appeal
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 17 — The High Court today allowed businessman and cosmetics entrepreneur and social media personality Datuk Seri Aliff Syukri Kamaruzaman’s bid to defer his apology to veteran politician Tan Sri Abdul Kadir Sheikh Fadzir in a RM30 million investment debt suit. Aliff Syukri’s lawyer, Mahmud Abdul Jumaat, confirmed the matter after proceedings on the stay of execution before Judge Roslan Mat Nor. On April 29, Judge Roslan ordered Aliff Syukri to pay RM250,000 to former Minister of Culture, Arts and Tourism Abdul Kadir, after allowing the suit filed by Abdul Kadir against him.

items.title: 1MDB ex-CEO Shahrol says no deal to escape US$5.64b civil suit, no explanation given too
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 17 — Former 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) chief executive officer (CEO) Datuk Shahrol Azral Ibrahim Halmi told the High Court today he has no idea why the company dropped him from its US$5.64 billion civil suit. He revealed this during cross-examination by lawyer G.K. Ganesan, who represents former 1MDB investment director Kelvin Tan Kay Jin, the seventh defendant in the suit. Shahrol Azral: Correct.

items.title: Fahmi: Pakatan leaders to meet on PKR congress and DAP conference outcomes
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 17 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) leaders will hold a meeting soon to discuss several matters identified following the PKR National Congress and DAP Party Conference, including efforts to accelerate reforms and address violations of the law and major scandals. PKR information chief Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the messages conveyed by delegates at the PKR congress and DAP members at the conference were clear that reform efforts must be expedited and firm action taken on issues involving breaches of the law and major scandals. “The message conveyed by the delegates at the Keadilan Congress and members at the DAP Conference was very clear that efforts to advance reforms must be accelerated and firm action must be taken, including on issues involving violations of the law and major scandals.

items.title: High Court to deliver ruling next February on Daim family bid to lift account freeze
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 17 — The High Court today fixed Feb 22, 2027 to deliver its decision on a judicial review application filed by the family of the late Tun Daim Zainuddin, seeking to lift the freeze on their bank accounts by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC). Judge Norliza Othman set the date after hearing submissions from lawyer Abraham Au, representing Daim’s family, while Senior Federal Counsel (SFC) Nurhafizza Azizan appeared for the MACC and five other respondents. Eighteen companies are also named as applicants, namely Aad Equity Sdn Bhd; Yayasan Haji Zainuddin; Ilham Baru Sdn Bhd; Anchor Point Sdn Bhd; Kangkung Catering Sdn Bhd; Adrihaniz Sdn Bhd; Syarikat Maluri Sdn Bhd; Amiraz Sdn Bhd; Ridana Sdn Bhd; Daan Sdn Bhd; Maya Seni Holdings Sdn Bhd; Magical Zone Sdn Bhd; Permatang Maju (M) Sdn Bhd; Brainstorms Sdn Bhd; Arida Farms Sdn Bhd; Gajah3 Resource Centre Sdn Bhd; Ilham Tower Sdn Bhd, and Selidik Jaya Sdn Bhd.

items.title: Judge rules Caprice defamed Ebit, orders apology and RM200,000 compensation
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Aug 17 — The Shah Alam Sessions Court today ordered social media personality Ariz Ramli, better known as Caprice, to pay RM200,000 in damages to preacher Ebit Irawan Ibrahim Lew in a defamation case. According to Free Malaysia Today (FMT), the ruling was delivered by Judge Zuhrina Nor, who found that Caprice had defamed the preacher in 2023 through seven statements made with Indonesian influencer Mondy Tattoo. The court granted a seven day ad interim stay on the damages payment to allow Caprice time to file a formal stay application, should he choose to appeal to the High Court.

items.title: Zahid chairs road safety panel, maps congestion fixes before Johor Bahru RTS January debut
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 17 — Plans are being drawn up to ease traffic congestion in Johor Bahru city centre and prevent new bottlenecks from emerging ahead of the launch of the Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link. Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the plans involved coordination among agencies and integration of public transport systems, as travel patterns were expected to change, particularly around the city centre and areas directly connected to the system. The system will connect Bukit Chagar in Johor Bahru with Woodlands North in Singapore.

items.title: No drug cartel in Genting: Pahang police stress immediate action if reports are lodged
items.summary: KUANTAN, Aug 17 — Pahang police have denied viral claims on social media that a large-scale drug cartel is operating in Genting Highlands, Bentong, without any enforcement action being taken. Acting Pahang police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob said police would conduct an investigation and take appropriate action if such illegal activity was detected. The social media user claimed that no action had been taken despite several police reports being lodged.

items.title: Alam Damai house goes up in flames, Bomba suspect EV charging in foyer the cause
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 17 — A two-storey terrace house in Alam Damai, Cheras, here, was destroyed in a fire early yesterday morning believed to have been caused by an electric vehicle (EV) that was being charged in the foyer of the house. Kuala Lumpur Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) operations division assistant director Ahmad Mukhlis Mukhtar in a statement today said his department received an emergency call regarding the incident at 5.03 am before a team of personnel from the Cheras, Sungai Besi and Bandar Tun Razak Fire and Rescue Stations (BBP) were rushed to the location. Ahmad Mukhlis said upon arriving at the location of the incident, his department found that the two-storey terrace house was 100 per cent burnt down.

items.title: Ex‑JKR officer tells High Court Muhyiddin made no calls to help Nepturis in RM141m Jana Wibawa project
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 17 — A former senior Public Works Department (JKR) officer today said he did not receive any phone calls from then prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin to help the contractor of a RM141 million government project, the High Court heard today. Former Selangor JKR director Lokman Nasir, 62, said this while testifying as the 23rd prosecution witness in Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia president Muhyiddin’s power abuse and money laundering trial. Lokman was in charge of supervising progress on the RM141 million project to build the Klang Utara district police headquarters (IPD), which was won by contractor Nepturis Sdn Bhd.

items.title: Sabah sets aside nearly RM1b to unlock state agriculture, industry and tourism potential
items.summary: KENINGAU, Aug 17 — The Sabah State Government has allocated nearly RM1 billion for the development of the agricultural, industrial and tourism sectors which continue to be among the main drivers of Sabah’s economic growth this year. In this regard, Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor wants district officers to look into the economic potential in their respective areas. Some have tourism potential.

items.title: Royal death brings early closure to Kelantan Heritage Weapons Festival in Kota Bharu
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Aug 17 — The Kelantan Heritage Weapons Festival 2026 has been closed today following the death of a member of the Kelantan royal family. The closure follows the death of the aunt of the Sultan of Kelantan Sultan Muhammad V, Datuk Tengku Salwani Almarhum Sultan Yahya Petra, at 6.10 am this morning at the age of 82. Confirmation of the death was made through the Sultan of Kelantan’s Office in a statement here today.

items.title: Sabah Heart Centre given top priority, Dzulkefly concedes staffing shortage remains a challenge
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Aug 17 — Construction of the RM125 million Sabah Heart Centre is expected to begin in the third quarter of next year, with the facility targeted for completion and operation by the third quarter of 2029, Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said today. The project is among seven new health projects approved for Sabah under RMK-13 Rolling Plan 1, which has allocated RM1.57 billion for 53 health projects in the state, including 46 ongoing projects and seven new projects. Dzulkefly said the Heart Centre would be given top priority by the Health Ministry, with the RM125 million allocation covering the overall project, including upgrading works, equipment procurement and related preliminary works.

items.title: Road crashes cost Malaysia up to RM30b a year, but human cost of 18 daily deaths is far greater, says minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 17 — Malaysia incurs up to RM30 billion in socio-economic losses each year due to road accidents, said Works Minister Dato Sri Alexander Nanta Linggi. Nanta said the findings on the socio-economic impact of road accidents were presented at the Cabinet Committee on Road Safety and Congestion meeting chaired by Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi. He said that last year alone, road accidents claimed 6,537 lives, equivalent to an average of 18 deaths a day.

items.title: Ministry defends transfer of Sabah hospital director amid ongoing sexual harassment probe
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Aug 17 — The Health Ministry’s decision to remove a Sabah hospital director from his post and transfer him to the state health department is pending further investigation into allegations of sexual harassment. Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad said the administrative transfer was made deliberately to ensure the investigation could proceed without the officer remaining in a position that could potentially affect the process. His comments came after the hospital director’s lawyer, Joan Goh, said he was mulling taking legal action over the transfer.

items.title: O&G sevice provider Alam Maritim Resources says CEO Azmi Ahmad under MACC remand
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 17 — Alam Maritim Resources Bhd today announced that its group managing director and group chief executive officer Datuk Azmi Ahmad is under remand to facilitate an ongoing investigation by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC). The service provider to the oil and gas industry said the remand is for the purpose of facilitating the ongoing investigation and does not constitute any finding of wrongdoing. “The board has taken the necessary measures to ensure continuity of the group’s operations and will make further announcements should there be any material development,” it said in a filing with Bursa Malaysia.

items.title: Baby Eden’s arrival makes Mahathir great‑grandfather, Ally Mukhriz celebrates newborn online
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Aug 17 — A new chapter has begun in the storied Mahathir family, as Ally Mukhriz — daughter of Parti Pejuang Tanah Air president Datuk Seri Mukhriz Mahathir — has given birth to her first child, a baby boy named Eden Zakaria Ezran Cheah. Born on Sunday morning at 8.48am, weighing 2.9kg, Eden is not only Ally and her husband Ezran Daud Cheah’s first child, but also the very first great grandchild of former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad and his wife Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohd Ali. Ally, whose full name is Meera Alyanna Mukhriz, shared the joyful news on Threads: “Ezran and I are happy to announce the birth of our baby boy, Eden Zakaria Ezran Cheah.

items.title: DOE: Air quality mostly moderate nationwide, Johan Setia stands out with unhealthy reading 137
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Aug 17 — Johan Setia in Selangor recorded an Air Pollutant Index (API) of 137 at 1pm today, the only location nationwide to report unhealthy air quality, the Department of Environment (DOE) said in a statement. The DOE said it had intensified patrols and drone monitoring in Johan Setia but found no open burning. The DOE said overall inspections found conditions in Johan Setia were under control, with no open burning detected at the time.

items.title: Room to grow: 524 classroom projects worth RM668m in the works for 2027
items.summary: KUALA NERUS, Aug 17 — A total of 524 additional classroom projects worth RM668 million are underway nationwide for the Year One intake in the 2027 session, said Deputy Works Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Maslan. Kedah followed with 93 (92 approved), while Johor recorded 47 (45 approved). “Terengganu has 45 projects and Penang 30, all with LoAs.

items.title: Malaysia Airlines pilots cleared in drug tests, MAG moves to cabin crew screening phase
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 17 — Malaysia Aviation Group (MAG) has completed a mandatory drug screening for all Malaysia Airlines pilots, with every test returning negative, the company said in a statement today. MAG said the exercise, concluded on August 15, covered all operationally active pilots. The group will now begin screening approximately 2,840 Malaysia Airlines cabin crew, starting August 18 and targeted for completion by September 3.

items.title: UUCA repeal can give Malaysian universities room to compete globally, says local varsitities
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 17 — The country’s new higher education legal framework must provide a conducive environment for Malaysian universities to grow, remain competitive and achieve excellence on par with leading institutions worldwide. International Islamic University Malaysia (IIUM) Rector Professor Emeritus Datuk Seri Dr Osman Bakar said the framework should be progressive, fair and forward-looking, while safeguarding the sustainability and integrity of universities. He said the move to replace the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (AUKU) presented an important opportunity to establish such a framework and empower universities to respond to the changing demands of an increasingly dynamic higher education landscape.

items.title: Pahang police investigate vandalised Bukit Tinggi temple statue, but no CCTV, no witnesses
items.summary: KUANTAN, Aug 17 — Police have received three reports regarding the incident of a statue at a non-Muslim place of worship being vandalised in Bukit Tinggi, Bentong, yesterday. Pahang acting police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob said the three police reports were made by a 49-year-old security guard, a 45-year-old monk and a 41-year-old man. Meanwhile, Azry Akmar said his party viewed the incident seriously and investigations were still underway to identify the cause and the parties involved.

items.title: Don’t just scrap UUCA, use it to reshape Malaysia’s universities, says UTM VC
items.summary: He said UTM welcomed the aspirations of the Ministry of Higher Education (KPT) to implement the transformation in a comprehensive and responsible manner. “Therefore, higher education legislation must evolve in line with changing times, without neglecting institutional stability and public interest,” he said in a statement. He said the new higher education legal framework also needs to recognise the diversity of institutions including universities, university colleges, technical-focused institutions and private education providers that have different mandates and challenges.

items.title: Future of Likas Wetlands, one of world’s only two city mangrove Ramsar sites, hangs in balance with mega project next door
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Aug 17 — The Likas Wetlands – only two of its kind in the world located within a city and enjoys global Ramsar status – may cease to exist within 15 years if nothing is done to prevent polluted water from a nearby mega project infiltrating the 24-hectare gazetted site and killing the vegetation. Sabah Wetland Conservation Society President, Datuk Zainie Abdul Aucasa who sounded the alarm bell was apparently referring to massive development coming up in the vicinity near Hakka Hall in Likas. Zaini said the Society would not waver or fail from its commitment to preserving the mangroves in the KK wetlands and defending its Ramsar status, the wetlands equivalent of World Heritage site.

items.title: DAP delegates have spoken, respect their decision, Kon Yeow tells Rafizi over unity govt stance
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 17 — DAP central executive committee member Chow Kon Yeow today told Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli to respect the party and its delegates’ decision to remain in the unity government. Chow said this was a basic principle following Rafizi’s comments on the resolution adopted at DAP’s congress yesterday. “We ask Rafizi to respect DAP and the decision of its delegates.

items.title: Penang’s undersea tunnel still on the map, draft plan keeps idea alive for 2040
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 17 — The proposed undersea tunnel or third bridge linking Penang island to the mainland was included as an indicative proposal in the Draft Penang State Structure Plan 2040 (RSN Penang 2040), Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said today. He said the project remain in the draft plan as the agreement with the appointed company is still valid, although its eventual implementation would depend on development schedules. He said the draft RSN Penang 2040 should serve as a “compass” for the state’s development.
